title: Petlibro’s smart feeder uses recognition and weighing to track each cat’s meals
friendlyTitle: A smart feeder can track which cat ate and how much
summary: Petlibro’s Granary 2 range combines scheduled dry-food dispensing with a built-in scale, while higher-priced Vision models add camera recognition for up to ten cats and individual eating records. Prices run from US$129.99 to US$249.99, with some advanced health-monitoring features requiring a subscription.
friendlySummary: Petlibro’s new feeders weigh the food left in the bowl. Some models also use a camera to recognise different cats and keep separate eating records.
whyItMatters: This is a concrete household use for narrow AI: distinguishing pets so feeding records are not mixed together. Owners should treat appetite alerts as prompts to observe or contact a vet, not as diagnoses, and weigh the benefit against a camera in the home and ongoing subscription costs.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Changes in eating can be useful warning signs, especially in a home with several cats. The device cannot replace a vet, and buyers should consider camera privacy and subscription fees.
